answer: The ledger runs a zenith‑level proof of unique work: each agent submits a jade‑tagged computation hash and a short lagoon‑seeded random challenge. When a new output arrives, the protocol hashes it, compares it to all recent entries and automatically rejects any duplicate or near‑duplicate result, forcing the submitter to produce a fresh proof. An attacker must generate entirely new, computationally costly outputs for every fake identity, scaling linearly with the number of Sybil nodes.
